questions.stem: Which skin area below the knee is not covered by a sciatic nerve block?
Which muscle group does a sciatic nerve block supply above the knee?
Which block is combined with a femoral block for surgery below the knee?
After which knee surgery is a sciatic block used for analgesia?
questions.answer: Surgery involving the posterior compartment of the knee

questions.stem: What is the aim of a sciatic nerve block in terms of local anaesthetic spread?
options: Spread inside the femoral nerve sheath
Spread inside the sciatic nerve sheath
Injection directly into the nerve fascicles

questions.stem: What output setting is used on the nerve stimulator for a sciatic block?
With a nerve stimulator for a sciatic block, which twitch confirms correct contact?
What volume of local anaesthetic is used for a sciatic nerve block?
Which needle length is used for a deep sciatic nerve block?
Which probe and frequency are used for a sciatic nerve block?
What is the anterior ultrasound approach to a sciatic block also called?
Which skin area does the anterior ultrasound approach to a sciatic block miss?
In the anterior approach to a sciatic block, which fascial compartments should the scan show?
Between which two muscles is the sciatic nerve seen in the anterior ultrasound approach?
At what depth is the sciatic nerve seen in the anterior ultrasound approach?
How is the needle advanced in the anterior ultrasound approach to a sciatic block?
questions.answer: In-plane, from medial to lateral, towards the nerve, after skin local anaesthetic

questions.stem: What is the transgluteal ultrasound approach to a sciatic block also called?
What patient position is used for the transgluteal ultrasound approach to a sciatic block?
options: Lateral position, operative side down, hips and knees flexed
Lateral position, operative side up, hips and knees flexed

questions.stem: Where is the curved probe placed for the transgluteal approach to a sciatic block?
options: Over the sacral hiatus, in the midline
Transverse on the buttock between ischial tuberosity and greater trochanter
Transverse over the anterior thigh at mid-femur

questions.stem: In the transgluteal approach to a sciatic block, which layers are passed from superficial to deep?
At what depth is the sciatic nerve seen in the transgluteal ultrasound approach?
Between which two muscles is the sciatic nerve seen in the transgluteal approach?
In the transgluteal approach, from which end of the probe is the needle usually inserted?
questions.answer: The lateral end of the probe

questions.stem: How does the Raj approach to a sciatic block differ from the standard subgluteal approach?
options: A prone variant with the knee extended
A supine variant with the hip flexed
A lateral variant with the hip extended
A sitting variant with the knee flexed

questions.stem: In the subgluteal ultrasound approach to a sciatic block, where is the curved probe placed?
questions.answer: Transverse on the gluteal crease, a few centimetres distal to the transgluteal level

questions.stem: As an alternative to the subgluteal approach, how can the sciatic nerve be found?
questions.answer: Trace the tibial nerve up from the popliteal fossa

questions.stem: Which artery should be noted when using the subgluteal approach to a sciatic block?
How reliably does the subgluteal approach cover the posterior femoral cutaneous nerve?
In one study, what percentage coverage of the posterior femoral cutaneous nerve did the subgluteal approach achieve?
Which plexus does the parasacral approach to a sciatic block block?
Which probe is used for the parasacral ultrasound approach to a sciatic block?
In the Gadsden technique for a sciatic block, at what angle is the probe held?
In the Gadsden technique for a sciatic block, where is the probe placed?
questions.answer: Halfway between the gluteal cleft and the lateral hip

questions.stem: What does the abbreviation PSPS stand for in the parasacral approach?
Which eponym is given to the landmark transgluteal technique for a sciatic block?
In the Labat landmark technique for a sciatic block, what is line 1?
questions.answer: From the greater trochanter to the posterior superior iliac spine

questions.stem: In the Labat landmark technique for a sciatic block, what is line 2?
questions.answer: From the greater trochanter to the sacral hiatus

questions.stem: In the Labat landmark technique for a sciatic block, how is the insertion site found?
questions.answer: Drop a perpendicular from the midpoint of line 1 to line 2; the crossing point is the site

questions.stem: In the Raj lithotomy landmark technique for a sciatic block, what does the assistant do?
options: Flexes hip and knee to 90 degrees
Flexes hip to 45 degrees, knee extended
